# shop

A Go web service generated by [gobento](https://github.com/Tales-of-zuna/gobento).

## Run

```sh
go run ./cmd/shop
```

The server listens on port 8080; set `PORT` to change it. It connects to the
database named by `DATABASE_URL`, as described in [Database](#database).

```sh
curl localhost:8080/health
curl -X POST localhost:8080/items -d '{"name":"first"}'
curl localhost:8080/items
```

## Test

```sh
go test ./...
```

## Layout

The code is organized by feature (a vertical slice) rather than by layer:
everything about items lives under `internal/items`, and code that every
feature shares lives under `internal/platform`.

| Directory | Contents |
|---|---|
| `cmd/shop` | Entry point: configuration and wiring |
| `internal/items` | The items feature: the `Item` type and the `ItemStore` interface |
| `internal/items/itemshttp` | The feature's HTTP handlers, plus the router and `/health` |
| `internal/items/itemsstore` | The feature's data access, implementing `ItemStore` |
| `internal/platform/database` | Database connection and schema, shared by all features |

Dependencies point inward: `itemshttp` and
`itemsstore` import `items`, never each
other, and `items` imports neither. Only
`cmd/shop` knows every package and connects them.

### Adding a feature

To add, for example, orders next to items:

1. Create `internal/orders` with the `Order` type and an `OrderStore`
   interface.
2. Add `internal/orders/ordershttp` with its handlers and
   `internal/orders/ordersstore` implementing `OrderStore`, following the
   items packages. Add its tables to the schema in
   `internal/platform/database`.
3. In `cmd/shop/main.go`, create the store and combine the
   routers in `newHandler`, for example with an `http.ServeMux` that sends
   `/orders` to the orders handlers and the other API paths to
   the items handlers.

A feature never imports another feature's subpackages. If orders need items,
depend on the `items` package and its interfaces.

## API

| Request | Response |
|---|---|
| `GET /health` | `200` with `{"status":"ok"}` |
| `GET /items` | `200` with a JSON array of items, oldest first |
| `POST /items` with `{"name":"..."}` | `201` with the created item |

Errors are JSON objects such as `{"error":"name is required"}`:

- `400` when the body is not exactly one JSON object with a non-empty `name`
  (unknown fields and data after the object are rejected);
- `413` when the body is larger than 1 MiB;
- `500` when storage fails. The details are logged, not sent to the client.

Routes are registered on a [chi](https://go-chi.io) router in
`internal/items/itemshttp/router.go`. Handlers are plain `http.HandlerFunc`s,
so any `net/http` middleware, including chi's own
[`middleware`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware)
package, can be added with `r.Use(...)`.

## Database

The application stores its data in PostgreSQL, through the pure-Go driver
[pgx](https://github.com/jackc/pgx) and `database/sql`, so it builds without a
C compiler. `DATABASE_URL` is a `postgres://` URL or a `key=value` connection
string. When it is unset, the application uses `DefaultURL` in
`internal/platform/database`, a local development server:

```text
postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/shop?sslmode=disable
```

Start such a server with Docker, or use any PostgreSQL server and set
`DATABASE_URL` to it:

```sh
docker run --rm -d --name shop-postgres -p 5432:5432 \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -e POSTGRES_DB=shop postgres:18-alpine
```

Stop it with `docker stop shop-postgres`; its data is deleted with
it.

### Tests

The database and store tests need a PostgreSQL server. They are skipped,
and `go test ./...` still passes, unless `TEST_DATABASE_URL` is set to a
`postgres://` URL. Each test then works in a schema of its own on that server,
which it drops when it ends, so the tests never touch the application's tables:

```sh
TEST_DATABASE_URL='postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/shop?sslmode=disable' go test ./...
```

Run `go test -v ./...` to see which tests were skipped. The CI workflow
starts a PostgreSQL service and sets `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, so these tests run
on every pull request.

### Schema

`internal/platform/database/schema.sql` is embedded in the binary and applied
every time the application starts. It uses `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, so it
creates missing tables but never changes existing ones: it is not a migration
system. Before you change the schema of a database that already holds data,
add a migration tool or change the existing tables by hand.

## Data access with GORM

The store in `internal/items/itemsstore` uses [GORM](https://gorm.io/) on the
connection opened by `internal/platform/database`. The tables are defined only in
`internal/platform/database/schema.sql`; the store does not
call `AutoMigrate`, so the schema file stays the single source of truth. When
you add a column, add it to the schema and to the struct in
`internal/items/itemsstore/store.go`.

## Development

`make` lists the tasks of the `Makefile`. Each one runs plain `go` or
`docker` commands, so without make (for example on Windows) run the command
next to it instead:

| Task | With make | Without make |
|---|---|---|
| Build the binary into `bin/` | `make build` | `go build -o bin/shop ./cmd/shop` |
| Run the server | `make run` | `go run ./cmd/shop` |
| Run the tests | `make test` | `go test ./...` |
| Run the tests with coverage | `make cover` | `go test -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...` |
| Vet the code | `make vet` | `go vet ./...` |
| Lint and check formatting | `make lint` | `go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.15.0 run` |
| Format the code | `make fmt` | `go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.15.0 fmt` |
| Tidy `go.mod` and `go.sum` | `make tidy` | `go mod tidy` |
| Run vet, lint, and the tests | `make check` | the three commands above |
| Build the container image | `make docker-build` | `docker build --tag shop .` |
| Run the container image | `make docker-run` | `docker run --rm --publish 8080:8080 shop` |

On Windows, `go build` needs `-o bin/shop.exe`; `make build` adds the
`.exe` itself. The linter's configuration is in `.golangci.yml`.

### Docker

The `Dockerfile` builds a static binary with cgo disabled and copies it into
a distroless image, which has no shell or package manager and runs the
server as the non-root user 65532 on port 8080. Building needs BuildKit, the
default builder of Docker 23 and later. The image reads `PORT` and
`DATABASE_URL` like the binary; `make docker-run DATABASE_URL=...` passes a
connection string to it.

Inside the container, `localhost` is the container itself, so the default
`DATABASE_URL` finds no server. Pass the server's address; a server on the
Docker host, such as the one started above, is `host.docker.internal`, which
`make docker-run` maps to the host:

```sh
make docker-run DATABASE_URL='postgres://postgres:postgres@host.docker.internal:5432/shop?sslmode=disable'
```

Without make, add `--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway` and
`--env DATABASE_URL=...` to `docker run`. A firewall on the host must let the
container reach the server's port; a server in another container is easier to
reach on a shared Docker network.

### Continuous integration

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every pull request and every push to
`main`. It checks that `go.mod` and `go.sum` are tidy, builds, vets, lints,
and runs the tests with the race detector, and it builds the container
image. Its actions are pinned by commit SHA, and the runtime image by
digest; `.github/dependabot.yml` keeps them, and the Go modules, up to date.
